item.description: In New South Wales, Australia, carbon credits have played a role in making the Great Koala National Park possible. Further details about the process or background are not provided in the source.

item.description: Xie Junwu, a wheelchair athlete from Nanchang, has climbed mountains, run marathons and now skateboards. At 19, he fell from a tree during a geology internship and became paralyzed from the waist down. item.title: Police officer donates rare anti-D blood 545 times across all 85 Australian blood banks
item.description: Trevor Bergman, a 59-year-old police officer from Melbourne, has donated rare anti-D antibodies in his blood 545 times across all 85 Australian donation centres, making him one of only 150 known Australians with this precious blood type. Anti-D is administered to pregnant women whose newborns are at risk of haemolytic disease. Bergman got the idea during a holiday in Perth...

item.description: In the English village of Botton, part of the Esk Valley Camphill Community in the North York Moors, people with and without learning disabilities live together as a community rather than as care provider and care recipient. item.title: Sardinian restaurants ban phones during family dinners
item.description: Restaurants in Sardinia are introducing a ban on phone use for families during meals. The idea is that families without screens will engage more in conversation with each other and pay more attention to one another and the meal. The story was published by The Optimist Daily, a news site focused on positive news, in the Nutrition & Wellness category.

item.title: California legalizes balcony solar panels for renters
item.description: California has legalized balcony solar energy. This means that renters and other residents can now attach solar panels to their balconies to generate their own electricity. The measure makes it possible for more people to access solar energy, even if they don't own their own roof or home. item.description: Five years ago, 18-year-old Kenli Riney lost her life in a head-on collision on a Texas highway, her car engulfed in flames. item.description: The Atlanta-based Star-C Program, founded by real estate owner Marjy Stagmeier, has helped more than 5,500 families keep their rental homes through its Eviction Relief Fund. item.title: Portuguese island Corvo turns off lights for shearwaters
item.description: On the Portuguese island of Corvo in the Azores, all street lights are switched off every year in late October for five nights, from 9 p.m. to 4 a.m. This protects young seabirds such as Cory's shearwater, which leave their nests at night to fly out to sea but become disoriented by artificial light and crash. item.title: New Agua Dulce nature reserve protects Iténez river as 'link of life'
item.description: Rainforest Trust has helped establish the 715,000-hectare Agua Dulce Municipal Wildlife Reserve along the Iténez river in Bolivia, described by scientists as a 'link of life'. The area is home to jaguars, Amazon river dolphins, giant otters, lowland tapirs, black caimans and 260 fish species, 25 of which are found nowhere else. item.description: While heat and drought affected crops worldwide this year, Japan's Hokkaido island experienced its best potato harvest in a decade.
